To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the RecA/RAD51-family proteins form a novel extended DNA conformation, and that this conformation is the key to understanding the homology search during homologous genetic recombinaton.

the extended DNA structure induced by a RecA/Radi family protein is a dynamic DNA structure that confers the ability to form a heteroduplex, and that the 2′-methylene-base interaction is essential to this dynamic property.

the extended DNA structure is the basis of the homology-search mechanism of the heterodupplex joint formation by a RecA/Rads1-family protein and that the dynamic property of this extended structure is the basis for the homologous genetic-recombination reaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a new concept of DNA as a dynamic molecule, in which the 2′ hydroxyl of RNA is replaced by the 2′ deoxyribose methylene, and the 2′-hydroxyl-base interaction in RNA is replaced by a 2′-methylene-base interaction in DNA.
the mechanism of homologous recombina-tion and the evolutionary advantage of DNA over its RNA counterpart.
the molecular basis of the genetic recombination, a key process in evolution, and has provided a new perspective on the evolutionary advantage of DNA over the RNA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the RecA/RAD51 family of proteins has evolved to utilize the 2′-methylenes of DNA, and the resulting extended DNA structure is a key to the evolution of DNA genomes.

DNA is more advantageous than RNA as genomic material, because DNA can form a novel extended structure, which allows the formation of hetero-duplex joints and the subsequent gene segment rearrangments.
the 2′-hydroxyl group of RNA makes the RNA genome more stable than DNA but less dynamic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the RecA/Rads1-family protein is a molecular switch that converts a static double-stranded DNA structure into a dynamic structure, and that this switch is the key to the success of DNA genomes in the evolution of organisms.
the RecA/RAD51-family proteins have evolved in order to utilize the unique property of DNA to promote the evolution of organisms.
DNA is a better genomic material than RNA, because of its dynamic property.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 2′-methylene-base interaction is the key to the dynamic property of DNA, which is not found in RNA.
the 2′-hydroxymethyl group is an important factor for the formation of heterologous DNA duplexes.
DNA is more flexible than RNA in terms of genetic recombination.
